title: Transitions & signal words Practice 1
description: 4 short texts - 8 focused transitions & signal words questions
subject: rla
passage:
TEXT A - Community Garden

The garden added two raised beds near the entrance. wheelchair users can reach more planting space without crossing uneven ground.

TEXT B - Battery Bus

Electric buses produce no tailpipe exhaust while operating. their batteries still require electricity to charge.

TEXT C - Museum Audio

The museum offers written labels in three languages. visitors can borrow an audio guide with additional descriptions.

TEXT D - Rain Barrel

A rain barrel can store water from a small roof. a large storm may fill it quickly.

questions.prompt: Which transition best connects these ideas? "The garden added two raised beds near the entrance. _____, wheelchair users can reach more planting space without crossing uneven ground."
questions.explanation: The second sentence describes a consequence of adding accessible raised beds near the entrance.
questions.rule: Name the relationship first, then prove it with the surrounding text.

options.whyWrong: However signals contrast, but the second idea follows positively from the first.
The second sentence is an effect of the change, not an example of raised beds.
This signals timing/addition and misses the cause-result relationship.

questions.prompt: What relationship should the transition signal?
questions.explanation: The added beds lead to greater access, so the logical relationship is result.
questions.rule: Name the relationship first, then prove it with the surrounding text.

options.whyWrong: The ideas support each other rather than conflict.
Greater access is the consequence of the change, not an example of it.
The second idea is more specific than simple addition because it follows from the first.

questions.prompt: Which transition best connects these ideas? "Electric buses produce no tailpipe exhaust while operating. _____, their batteries still require electricity to charge."
questions.explanation: The first sentence gives a benefit, while the second qualifies it by noting the electricity required for charging.
questions.rule: Name the relationship first, then prove it with the surrounding text.

options.whyWrong: Battery charging is not presented as a consequence of having no tailpipe exhaust.
The second idea is a limitation, not an example of the first.
Likewise signals similarity, but the second idea qualifies the benefit.

questions.prompt: What relationship should the transition signal?
questions.explanation: The battery requirement limits an otherwise positive statement about operating emissions.
questions.rule: Name the relationship first, then prove it with the surrounding text.

options.whyWrong: The charging requirement is not caused by the lack of tailpipe exhaust.
It is a qualification, not an illustration.
The ideas are not simply parallel facts; the second limits the first.

questions.prompt: Which transition best connects these ideas? "The museum offers written labels in three languages. _____, visitors can borrow an audio guide with additional descriptions."
questions.explanation: The audio guide is another service offered alongside multilingual written labels.
questions.rule: Name the relationship first, then prove it with the surrounding text.

options.whyWrong: The audio guide supplements the labels rather than replacing them.
The passage does not say the written labels cause the audio guide.
The second sentence adds another resource instead of contrasting with the first.

questions.prompt: What relationship should the transition signal?
questions.explanation: The second sentence adds another accessibility resource to the first.
questions.rule: Name the relationship first, then prove it with the surrounding text.

options.whyWrong: The services do not conflict.
One service is not presented as the consequence of the other.
The audio guide is an additional option, not an example of written labels.

questions.prompt: Which transition best connects these ideas? "A rain barrel can store water from a small roof. _____, a large storm may fill it quickly."
questions.explanation: The second sentence introduces a limitation to the barrel's ability to store roof runoff.
questions.rule: Name the relationship first, then prove it with the surrounding text.

options.whyWrong: A large storm filling the barrel is not framed as a desired result of its storage ability.
The second sentence qualifies capacity rather than illustrating the first with an example.
The two sentences are not parallel similarities.

questions.prompt: What relationship should the transition signal?
questions.explanation: The second idea limits the usefulness described in the first.
questions.rule: Name the relationship first, then prove it with the surrounding text.

options.whyWrong: The relationship is not simply a consequence signal.
The storm is used to show a limitation, not merely an example.
Simple addition misses the tension between useful storage and limited capacity.

curriculum.learningObjective: Apply transitions & signal words reasoning across varied original texts and explain answers from textual evidence.
